title: CoordinationDeclaration
description: Normative shape of the coordination declaration, for connector/contracts/coordination-declaration@0.1.0. It is the open variability point of resource coordination: a connector author says which of a tool's own arguments name the things it may change, and how that platform's identifiers are spelled, and the coordinator does the rest without knowing anything about the platform. The two members are authored inside the connector manifest that connector/contracts/connector-manifest@1.2.0 defines - tool_coordination on a tool, connector_coordination on the manifest - and are read once, at registration, never from a call and never reloaded while the product runs. The bounds here are the measured ones: concurrency stops at eight because that is where eight concurrent jobs on one account produced refusals for volume at about five percent, and the wait limit is bounded so that a call cannot wait long enough for a person to think the product has stopped. What the file cannot express, and what the contract document holds instead: that a declared path exists in that tool's parameters, that a declared type means the same thing across the connector's tools, and that a resource genuinely covers everything the call changes - a declaration that names too little locks nothing while believing it has locked something.

tool_coordination.description: Required for every tool whose direction is write. A writing tool with no resources is refused, and with it the whole manifest.

connector_coordination.description: Absent means the product's defaults. A figure above the maximum is clamped to it and the clamp is reported to the connector's author rather than the manifest being refused.
